sanskrit: upavāsaiś ca vividhair dīkṣābhir niyamais tathā ātmano laghutāṃ kṛtvā babhūva mṛgacāriṇī
english: Through various fasts, consecrations, and vows, having made herself light in body, she became one who roamed with the deer.

sanskrit: vaiḍūryāṅkurakalpāni mṛdūni haritāni ca carantī śaṣpamukhyāni tiktāni madhurāṇi ca
english: She wandered about eating tender green shoots resembling beryl gemstones, the finest young grasses, both bitter and sweet.

sanskrit: sravantīnāṃ ca puṇyānāṃ surasāni śucīni ca pibantī vārimukhyāni śītāni vimalāni ca
english: And drinking the fragrant, pure, choicest waters of holy rivers — cold and crystal clear.

sanskrit: vaneṣu mṛgarājeṣu siṃhaviproṣiteṣu ca dāvāgnivipramukteṣu śūnyeṣu gahaneṣu ca
english: In forests where lions had once roamed and then departed, in thickets freed from forest fires, in desolate and dense groves —

sanskrit: carantī hariṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ mṛgīva vanacāriṇī cacāra vipulaṃ dharmaṃ brahmacaryeṇa saṃvṛtā
english: roaming with the deer like a doe ranging through the forest, she practiced great dharma, fully covered by the vow of brahmacharya.

sanskrit: yayātir api pūrveṣāṃ rājñāṃ vṛttam anuṣṭhitaḥ bahuvarṣasahasrāyur ayujat kāladharmaṇā
english: Yayāti too, having followed the conduct of kings of old, after a life spanning thousands of years, met the law of time — death.

sanskrit: pūrur yaduś ca dvau vaṃśau vardhamānau narottamau tābhyāṃ pratiṣṭhito loke paraloke ca nāhuṣaḥ
english: The two lineages of Pūru and Yadu, growing and foremost among men — through these two, the son of Nahuṣa was established in this world and the next.

sanskrit: mahīyate narapatir yayātiḥ svargam āsthitaḥ maharṣikalpo nṛpatiḥ svargāgryaphalabhug vibhuḥ
english: King Yayāti, having ascended to heaven, was honored — that king, equal to a great ṛṣi, the mighty one who enjoyed the foremost fruits of heaven.

sanskrit: bahuvarṣasahasrākhye kāle bahuguṇe gate rājarṣiṣu niṣaṇṇeṣu mahīyaḥsu maharṣiṣu
english: When a span of many thousands of years had passed, replete with virtues, and he sat amid honored royal seers and great sages —

sanskrit: avamene narān sarvān devān ṛṣigaṇāṃs tathā yayātir mūḍhavijñāno vismayāviṣṭacetanaḥ
english: Yayāti, his understanding obscured by folly, his mind seized by conceit, began to despise all men, gods, and hosts of seers.

sanskrit: tatas taṃ bubudhe devaḥ śakro balaniṣūdanaḥ te ca rājarṣayaḥ sarve dhig dhig ity evam abruvan
english: Then the god Śakra, slayer of Bala, became aware of him; and all those royal sages said, "Shame! Shame!" thus they spoke.

sanskrit: vicāraś ca samutpanno nirīkṣya nahuṣātmajam ko nv ayaṃ kasya vā rājñaḥ kathaṃ vā svargam āgataḥ
english: And a discussion arose as they looked upon the son of Nahuṣa: "Who is this? Of which king? How did he come to heaven?"

sanskrit: karmaṇā kena siddho 'yaṃ kva vānena tapaś citam kathaṃ vā jñāyate svarge kena vā jñāyate 'py uta
english: "By what deed has he attained this state? Where did he accumulate austerity? How is he known in heaven, and by whom is he known?"

sanskrit: evaṃ vicārayantas te rājānaḥ svargavāsinaḥ dṛṣṭvā papracchur anyonyaṃ yayātiṃ nṛpatiṃ prati
english: Thus deliberating, those kings dwelling in heaven, having seen him, questioned one another about King Yayāti.

sanskrit: vimānapālāḥ śataśaḥ svargadvārābhirakṣiṇaḥ pṛṣṭā āsanapālāś ca na jānīmety athābruvan
english: The hundreds of keepers of the celestial chariots, the guardians of heaven's gates, were asked — and so were the keepers of the thrones — and they replied: "We do not know."

sanskrit: sarve te hy āvṛtajñānā nābhyajānanta taṃ nṛpam sa muhūrtād atha nṛpo hataujā abhavat tadā
english: All of them, their knowledge veiled, did not recognize that king. Then after a moment the king's vigor was struck down.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca atha pracalitaḥ sthānād āsanāc ca paricyutaḥ kampitenaiva manasā dharṣitaḥ śokavahninā
english: Nārada said: Then he was dislodged from his place and fell from his seat, his mind trembling, assailed by the fire of grief.

sanskrit: mlānasragbhraṣṭavijñānaḥ prabhraṣṭamukuṭāṅgadaḥ vighūrṇan srastasarvāṅgaḥ prabhraṣṭābharaṇāmbaraḥ
english: His garland withered, his understanding departed, his crown and armlets fallen, he spun about with all his limbs slack, his ornaments and garments dropping away.

sanskrit: adṛśyamānas tān paśyann apaśyaṃś ca punaḥ punaḥ śūnyaḥ śūnyena manasā prapatiṣyan mahītalam
english: Becoming invisible to them as he gazed at them, and then unable to see them again and again, empty, with an empty mind, he was about to plunge to the earth.

sanskrit: kiṃ mayā manasā dhyātam aśubhaṃ dharmadūṣaṇam yenāhaṃ calitaḥ sthānād iti rājā vyacintayat
english: "What inauspicious thing, what corruption of dharma, did I contemplate in my mind, by which I have been dislodged from my place?" — thus the king reflected.

sanskrit: te tu tatraiva rājānaḥ siddhāś cāpsarasas tathā apaśyanta nirālambaṃ yayātiṃ taṃ paricyutam
english: And those kings, siddhas, and apsarases, still there in that place, saw Yayāti falling without support, dislodged.

sanskrit: athaitya puruṣaḥ kaś cit kṣīṇapuṇyanipātakaḥ yayātim abravīd rājan devarājasya śāsanāt
english: Then a certain person, the one who casts down those whose merit is exhausted, came and spoke to Yayāti by command of the king of gods:

sanskrit: atīva madamattas tvaṃ na kaṃ cin nāvamanyase mānena bhraṣṭaḥ svargas te nārhas tvaṃ pārthivātmaja na ca prajñāyase gaccha patasveti tam abravīt
english: "You are utterly intoxicated with pride; there is no one you do not despise. Fallen through arrogance, heaven is not for you, O son of an earthly king — you are not recognized. Go — fall!" Thus he addressed him.

sanskrit: pateyaṃ satsv iti vacas trir uktvā nahuṣātmajaḥ patiṣyaṃś cintayām āsa gatiṃ gatimatāṃ varaḥ
english: Having spoken thrice the words "May I fall among the virtuous," the son of Nahuṣa, as he was about to fall, reflected on a destination — he who was foremost among those with discernment.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu naimiṣe pārthivarṣabhān caturo 'paśyata nṛpas teṣāṃ madhye papāta saḥ
english: At that very moment, the king saw four foremost kings in Naimiṣa forest, and he fell down in their midst.

sanskrit: pratardano vasumanāḥ śibirauśīnaro 'ṣṭakaḥ vājapeyena yajñena tarpayanti sureśvaram
english: Pratardana, Vasumanā, Śibi of the Uśīnaras, and Aṣṭaka — they were satisfying the lord of the gods with the Vājapeya sacrifice.

sanskrit: teṣām adhvarajaṃ dhūmaṃ svargadvāram upasthitam yayātir upajighran vai nipapāta mahīṃ prati
english: Yayāti, inhaling the sacrificial smoke from their rite as it rose to the gate of heaven, fell down toward the earth.

sanskrit: bhūmau svarge ca saṃbaddhāṃ nadīṃ dhūmamayīṃ nṛpaḥ sa gaṅgām iva gacchantīm ālambya jagatīpatiḥ
english: That lord of the world, taking hold of the river of smoke — which connected earth and heaven and flowed like the Gaṅgā — descended.

sanskrit: śrīmatsv avabhṛthāgryeṣu caturṣu pratibandhuṣu madhye nipatito rājā lokapālopameṣu ca
english: The king fell into the midst of those four splendid kinsmen, who had just completed the final bath of their sacrifice and who were equal to guardians of the worlds.

sanskrit: caturṣu hutakalpeṣu rājasiṃhamahāgniṣu papāta madhye rājarṣir yayātiḥ puṇyasaṃkṣaye
english: The royal sage Yayāti, his merit exhausted, fell into the midst of those four, who were like oblation fires, like lions among kings, blazing greatly.

sanskrit: tam āhuḥ pārthivāḥ sarve pratimānam iva śriyaḥ ko bhavān kasya vā bandhur deśasya nagarasya vā
english: All those kings addressed him — he who was like an image of splendor: "Who are you? Whose kinsman? Of what land or city?"

sanskrit: yakṣo vāpy atha vā devo gandharvo rākṣaso 'pi vā na hi mānuṣarūpo 'si ko vārthaḥ kāṅkṣitas tvayā
english: "Are you a yakṣa, or a god, a gandharva, or perhaps a rākṣasa? You are not of human form. What purpose do you seek?"

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca yayātir asmi rājarṣiḥ kṣīṇapuṇyaś cyuto divaḥ pateyaṃ satsv iti dhyāyan bhavatsu patitas tataḥ
english: Yayāti said: I am Yayāti, the royal sage, fallen from heaven with my merit exhausted. Meditating on the words "May I fall among the virtuous," I fell here, among you.

sanskrit: rājāna ūcuḥ satyam etad bhavatu te kāṅkṣitaṃ puruṣarṣabha sarveṣāṃ naḥ kratuphalaṃ dharmaś ca pratigṛhyatām
english: The kings said: Let that which you desired be true, O bull among men. Let the fruit of all our sacrifices and the merit of our dharma be accepted by you.

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca nāhaṃ pratigrahadhano brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo hy aham na ca me praṇavā buddhiḥ parapuṇyavināśane
english: Yayāti said: I am no brahmin whose wealth is accepting gifts — I am a kṣatriya. Nor is my mind inclined toward the destruction of another's merit.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca etasminn eva kāle tu mṛgacaryākramāgatām mādhavīṃ prekṣya rājānas te 'bhivādyedam abruvan
english: Nārada said: At that very time, those kings, seeing Mādhavī who had come there in the course of her wandering with the deer, greeted her and said this:

sanskrit: kim āgamanakṛtyaṃ te kiṃ kurvaḥ śāsanaṃ tava ājñāpyā hi vayaṃ sarve tava putrās tapodhane
english: "What is the purpose of your coming? What shall we do? Your command — for we are all at your command, your sons, O you rich in austerity."

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tad bhāṣitaṃ śrutvā mādhavī parayā mudā pitaraṃ samupāgacchad yayātiṃ sā vavanda ca
english: Hearing their words, Mādhavī with great joy approached her father, and she bowed to Yayāti.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā mūrdhnā natān putrāṃs tāpasī vākyam abravīt dauhitrās tava rājendra mama putrā na te parāḥ ime tvāṃ tārayiṣyanti diṣṭam etat purātanam
english: Seeing her sons bowing their heads, the ascetic woman spoke these words: "Your grandsons, O king of kings, my own sons — they are not strangers to you. These will rescue you — this is the ancient decree of fate."

sanskrit: ahaṃ te duhitā rājan mādhavī mṛgacāriṇī mayāpy upacito dharmas tato 'rdhaṃ pratigṛhyatām
english: "I am your daughter, O king — Mādhavī, the one who roams with the deer. I too have accumulated merit; let half of that be accepted by you."

sanskrit: yasmād rājan narāḥ sarve apatyaphalabhāginaḥ tasmād icchanti dauhitrān yathā tvaṃ vasudhādhipa
english: "Because, O king, all men share in the fruit of their offspring, therefore they desire their daughter's sons — even as you do, O lord of the earth."

sanskrit: tatas te pārthivāḥ sarve śirasā jananīṃ tadā abhivādya namaskṛtya mātāmaham athābruvan
english: Then all those kings, bowing their heads in reverence to their mother, and paying homage, then spoke to their maternal grandfather:

sanskrit: uccair anupamaiḥ snigdhaiḥ svarair āpūrya medinīm mātāmahaṃ nṛpatayas tārayanto divaś cyutam
english: The kings, filling the earth with lofty, incomparable, affectionate voices, strove to rescue their maternal grandfather who had fallen from heaven.

sanskrit: atha tasmād upagato gālavo 'py āha pārthivam tapaso me 'ṣṭabhāgena svargam ārohatāṃ bhavān
english: Then Gālava, coming near, also spoke to that king: "Let Your Majesty ascend to heaven by an eighth part of my austerity."

sanskrit: nārada uvāca pratyabhijñātamātro 'tha sadbhis tair narapuṃgavaḥ yayātir divyasaṃsthāno babhūva vigatajvaraḥ
english: Nārada said: The very moment he was recognized by those virtuous men, that bull among men Yayāti assumed a divine form and became free of affliction.

sanskrit: divyamālyāmbaradharo divyābharaṇabhūṣitaḥ divyagandhaguṇopeto na pṛthvīm aspṛśat padā
english: Wearing a divine garland and divine garments, adorned with divine ornaments, endowed with divine fragrance, his feet no longer touched the earth.

sanskrit: tato vasumanāḥ pūrvam uccair uccārayan vacaḥ khyāto dānapatir loke vyājahāra nṛpaṃ tadā
english: Then Vasumanā, renowned in the world as the lord of generosity, spoke loudly first and addressed the king:

sanskrit: prāptavān asmi yal loke sarvavarṇeṣv agarhayā tad apy atha ca dāsyāmi tena saṃyujyatāṃ bhavān
english: "Whatever I have gained in this world through giving without censure to all classes of people — that I shall give; may you be joined with that merit."

sanskrit: yat phalaṃ dānaśīlasya kṣamāśīlasya yat phalam yac ca me phalam ādhāne tena saṃyujyatāṃ bhavān
english: "Whatever fruit belongs to one given to generosity, whatever fruit belongs to one given to forbearance, and whatever fruit I have in sacred deposits — may you be joined with that."

sanskrit: tataḥ pratardano 'py āha vākyaṃ kṣatriyapuṃgavaḥ yathā dharmaratir nityaṃ nityaṃ yuddhaparāyaṇaḥ
english: Then Pratardana, that bull among kṣatriyas, who was always devoted to dharma and always intent on battle, also spoke:

sanskrit: prāptavān asmi yal loke kṣatradharmodbhavaṃ yaśaḥ vīraśabdaphalaṃ caiva tena saṃyujyatāṃ bhavān
english: "Whatever glory arising from kṣatriya dharma I have gained in this world, and the fruit of being called a hero — may you be joined with that."

sanskrit: śibirauśīnaro dhīmān uvāca madhurāṃ giram yathā bāleṣu nārīṣu vaihāryeṣu tathaiva ca
english: Śibi of the Uśīnaras, the wise one, spoke sweet words: "Just as toward children, toward women, and toward the helpless —"

sanskrit: saṃgareṣu nipāteṣu tathāpad vyasaneṣu ca anṛtaṃ noktapūrvaṃ me tena satyena khaṃ vraja
english: "— in battles, in falls from fortune, in adversities and calamities alike — I have never previously spoken an untruth. By that truth, ascend to heaven."

sanskrit: yathā prāṇāṃś ca rājyaṃ ca rājan karma sukhāni ca tyajeyaṃ na punaḥ satyaṃ tena satyena khaṃ vraja
english: "As I would give up life, kingdom, action, and pleasures, O king, but never truth — by that truth, ascend to heaven."

sanskrit: yathā satyena me dharmo yathā satyena pāvakaḥ prītaḥ śakraś ca satyena tena satyena khaṃ vraja
english: "As my dharma rests on truth, as fire is pleased by truth, as Śakra is pleased by truth — by that truth, ascend to heaven."

sanskrit: aṣṭakas tv atha rājarṣiḥ kauśiko mādhavīsutaḥ anekaśatayajvānaṃ vacanaṃ prāha dharmavit
english: Then Aṣṭaka, the royal sage, the Kauśika, son of Mādhavī, the knower of dharma who had performed hundreds of sacrifices, spoke these words:

sanskrit: śataśaḥ puṇḍarīkā me gosavāś ca citāḥ prabho kratavo vājapeyāś ca teṣāṃ phalam avāpnuhi
english: "Hundreds of Puṇḍarīka sacrifices and Gosava rites have been performed by me, O lord, and Vājapeya sacrifices — receive the fruit of all these."

sanskrit: na me ratnāni na dhanaṃ na tathānye paricchadāḥ kratuṣv anupayuktāni tena satyena khaṃ vraja
english: "No jewels of mine, no wealth, nor any other possessions have remained unused in sacrifices. By that truth, ascend to heaven."

sanskrit: yathā yathā hi jalpanti dauhitrās taṃ narādhipam tathā tathā vasumatīṃ tyaktvā rājā divaṃ yayau
english: And as the grandsons spoke thus to that king, step by step, leaving the earth, the king ascended to heaven.

sanskrit: evaṃ sarve samastās te rājānaḥ sukṛtais tadā yayātiṃ svargato bhraṣṭaṃ tārayām āsur añjasā
english: Thus all those assembled kings, through their meritorious deeds, swiftly rescued Yayāti who had fallen from heaven.

sanskrit: dauhitrāḥ svena dharmeṇa yajñadānakṛtena vai caturṣu rājavaṃśeṣu saṃbhūtāḥ kulavardhanāḥ mātāmahaṃ mahāprājñaṃ divam āropayanti te
english: The grandsons, through their own dharma earned by sacrifice and gifts, born in four royal lineages and enhancers of their families, they lifted that supremely wise maternal grandfather to heaven.

sanskrit: rājāna ūcuḥ rājadharmaguṇopetāḥ sarvadharmaguṇānvitāḥ dauhitrās te vayaṃ rājan divam āroha pārthivaḥ
english: The kings said: Endowed with the qualities of royal dharma, possessed of all virtuous qualities, we are your grandsons, O king. Ascend to heaven, O earthly lord.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca sadbhir āropitaḥ svargaṃ pārthivair bhūridakṣiṇaiḥ abhyanujñāya dauhitrān yayātir divam āsthitaḥ
english: Nārada said: Lifted to heaven by those virtuous kings of great gifts, Yayāti took leave of his grandsons and ascended to the sky.

sanskrit: abhivṛṣṭaś ca varṣeṇa nānāpuṣpasugandhinā pariṣvaktaś ca puṇyena vāyunā puṇyagandhinā
english: He was showered with a rain of various fragrant flowers, and embraced by a pure, holy-scented wind.

sanskrit: acalaṃ sthānam āruhya dauhitraphalanirjitam karmabhiḥ svair upacito jajvāla parayā śriyā
english: Ascending to an immovable station won by the merit of his grandsons, enriched by his own deeds, he blazed with supreme splendor.

sanskrit: upagītopanṛttaś ca gandharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇaiḥ prītyā pratigṛhītaś ca svarge dundubhinisvanaiḥ
english: Sung to and danced around by hosts of gandharvas and apsarases, he was welcomed with joy in heaven to the sound of divine drums.

sanskrit: abhiṣṭutaś ca vividhair devarājarṣicāraṇaiḥ arcitaś cottamārgheṇa daivatair abhinanditaḥ
english: Praised with various eulogies by gods, royal sages, and cāraṇas, he was honored with the finest tribute and celebrated by the gods.

sanskrit: prāptaḥ svargaphalaṃ caiva tam uvāca pitāmahaḥ nirvṛtaṃ śāntamanasaṃ vacobhis tarpayann iva
english: Having attained the fruit of heaven, the Grandsire (Brahmā) spoke to him — who was content and of tranquil mind — as if satisfying him with words:

sanskrit: catuṣpādas tvayā dharmaś cito lokyena karmaṇā akṣayas tava loko 'yaṃ kīrtiś caivākṣayā divi punas tavādya rājarṣe sukṛteneha karmaṇā
english: "The four-footed dharma has been gathered by you through meritorious deeds. This world of yours is imperishable, and your fame in heaven imperishable — moreover, O royal sage, today through your good deed here."

sanskrit: āvṛtaṃ tamasā cetaḥ sarveṣāṃ svargavāsinām yena tvāṃ nābhijānanti tato 'jñātvāsi pātitaḥ
english: "The minds of all the dwellers in heaven had been veiled in darkness, by which they did not recognize you — thus, not being known, you were cast down."

sanskrit: prītyaiva cāsi dauhitrais tāritas tvam ihāgataḥ sthānaṃ ca pratipanno 'si karmaṇā svena nirjitam acalaṃ śāśvataṃ puṇyam uttamaṃ dhruvam avyayam
english: "And through the love of your grandsons you have been rescued and come here, and you have regained the station won by your own deeds — immovable, eternal, holy, supreme, permanent, and imperishable."

sanskrit: yayātir uvāca bhagavan saṃśayo me 'sti kaś cit taṃ chettum arhasi na hy anyam aham arhāmi praṣṭuṃ lokapitāmaha
english: Yayāti said: O Blessed One, there is a certain doubt in me; please resolve it. For there is no other I am fit to ask, O Grandsire of the worlds.

sanskrit: bahuvarṣasahasrāntaṃ prajāpālanavardhitam anekakratudānaughair arjitaṃ me mahat phalam
english: "The great fruit I had earned — spanning thousands upon thousands of years, built by the protection of subjects, accumulated through floods of sacrifices and gifts —"

sanskrit: kathaṃ tad alpakālena kṣīṇaṃ yenāsmi pātitaḥ bhagavan vettha lokāṃś ca śāśvatān mama nirjitān
english: "— how was that exhausted in so short a time, causing my fall? O Blessed One, you know the eternal worlds that I had won."

sanskrit: pitāmaha uvāca bahuvarṣasahasrāntaṃ prajāpālanavardhitam anekakratudānaughair yat tvayopārjitaṃ phalam
english: The Grandsire said: That great fruit you had earned — spanning thousands upon thousands of years, built by the protection of subjects, accumulated through floods of sacrifices and gifts —

sanskrit: tad anenaiva doṣeṇa kṣīṇaṃ yenāsi pātitaḥ abhimānena rājendra dhikkṛtaḥ svargavāsibhiḥ
english: "— that was exhausted by this very fault by which you were cast down: by arrogance, O king of kings, you were condemned by the dwellers in heaven."

sanskrit: nāyaṃ mānena rājarṣe na balena na hiṃsayā na śāṭhyena na māyābhir loko bhavati śāśvataḥ
english: "This eternal world, O royal sage, is not won by pride, nor by force, nor by violence, nor by cunning, nor by deceit."

sanskrit: nāvamānyās tvayā rājann avarotkṛṣṭamadhyamāḥ na hi mānapradagdhānāṃ kaś cid asti samaḥ kva cit
english: "The inferior, the exalted, and the middling are not to be despised by you, O king. For among those burned by contempt, there is no one who is at peace anywhere."

sanskrit: patanārohaṇam idaṃ kathayiṣyanti ye narāḥ viṣamāṇy api te prāptās tariṣyanti na saṃśayaḥ
english: "Those men who shall recount this fall and rising again — even when they encounter adversities, they will cross over them without doubt."

sanskrit: nārada uvāca eṣa doṣo 'bhimānena purā prāpto yayātinā nirbandhataś cātimātraṃ gālavena mahīpate
english: Nārada said: This is the fault that was incurred long ago by Yayāti through arrogance, and also by Gālava through excessive insistence, O lord of the earth.
